overall_design: Split the cancellation impetus across Pierre’s dinner email and a separate conference status page. Pierre’s email supplies the operation (“cancel the London AI Summit event”) and a link to the conference page. The linked page confirms the summit cancellation, identifies it by name and date, but deliberately omits the calendar event ID. This forces the assistant to search the calendar for ‘London AI Summit’ to locate the correct entry, satisfying the target tool sequence while keeping the decision to cancel rooted in the email’s last‑minute note.

site_plans.plan: Local role: dependency and operation trigger. Add a short trailing paragraph in Pierre’s voice: ‘P.S. – Just heard the London AI Summit scheduled for 27 May has been cancelled. Can you also remove the calendar event for it? The official notice is here: {URL}.’ Do not specify the event ID or the cancellation tool; only cue the need, point to the conference page, and blend naturally after the restaurant request.
Local role: exact conference‑notice URL only. Keep it short and plausible, e.g. ‘https://londonaisummit.org/2024/status’, without any instructional text.

Local role: identity confirmation and cancellation record. Display a short notice: ‘London AI Summit – 27 May 2024 – CANCELLED. Please delete any associated calendar entries.’ Include no event ID, so the next natural step is to search the user’s calendar for the summit name.
